sections.h2: Is a fast sale possible in Falls Township, PA?
sections.html:
It is. Falls Township owners can use an agent, handle the sale themselves, or accept cash from a buyer who takes the house as it is. The township asks for no home inspection, though a few resale steps must still be completed before closing.

Falls is a suburban Philadelphia township on the Delaware in Bucks County. Portions of Fairless Hills and Levittown are inside it, and a few addresses carry a Morrisville or Yardley mailing name though they lie in Falls. Residents numbered 34,716 in the 2020 Census and an estimated 34,282 by July 2025, down 1.3%.

The township was chartered in 1692. Morrisville left it to become a borough in 1804, and Tullytown followed in 1891. Fallsington, a crossroads village, has stayed in continuous use since the colonial era. William Penn started building his Pennsbury Manor residence here in 1682, and the reconstructed site is open to the public.

Population stood at 3,540 in 1950 and 29,082 in 1960 as Fairless Hills and Levittown were built. Details a buyer will check:

  • Land and water: 26.6 square miles in total, 22.3 of land and 4.3 of water (16.11%), with Biles Island, Martins Creek and Queen Anne Creek among the features.
  • Highways: US 1 is a freeway across the north, US 13 follows the old King's Highway, and PA 32 starts at US 1 in the northeast corner.
  • Rail and bus: the Amtrak Northeast Corridor and SEPTA Trenton Line cross the township without a station in it. Levittown station is the nearest, and SEPTA buses 127 and 128 serve Falls.
  • Road upkeep: the township maintains 85.88 of its 131.48 public road miles.

sections.h2: What do the numbers say about Falls Township homes?
sections.html:
A typical owner's home in Falls was worth $361,900 for 2020 to 2024, and owners occupy 72.9% of homes. Households earn a median $93,223, and median gross rent is $1,465.

sections.h2: What must a Falls Township house pass before it is resold?
sections.html:
Four major components have to be certified before Falls issues a certificate of occupancy for a resale, and no township home inspection is required. A 2021 ordinance swapped the older resale inspection for certification of the heating system, chimney, sewer system and electrical panel. When the ordinance passed in January 2021, the township manager said a buyer's private inspection goes "far greater" than the township's, and that buyers are told of open violations or outstanding permit violations before they buy.

  • Who handles it: the Code Enforcement Department, which schedules use and occupancy, electrical and housing inspections and also takes permit applications.
  • Rentals: the ordinance also created a rental inspection program: apartment complexes get a yearly look at common areas, and any unit occupied three years or more gets an interior inspection.
  • Historic area: a Historic Architectural Review Board takes requests for review of plans, so ask whether your property falls under it.
  • Flood paperwork: the township posts a flood hazard area permit application and a FEMA substantial improvement form, relevant to a house near the river or a creek.

Ask the Code Enforcement Department which components your house must certify and whether any permit on the property was left open.

sections.h2: Does water or storm history matter in a Falls Township sale?
sections.html:
Buyers will ask about drainage and flood history, since water covers about 16% of the township and the climate station sits at 13 feet above sea level. Average precipitation is 47.78 inches a year, July is the wettest month, and the heaviest day since 1981 was August 27, 2011, at 6.49 inches. The warmest reading in that period, 103.4 degrees, came on June 7, 2010. Winter can bite as well: the coldest reading since 1981 was minus 10.2 degrees on January 22, 1984, in a township that sits in hardiness zone 7a, so the age of a heating system is a fair buyer question. The township also holds the easternmost point of Pennsylvania's southern half, a detail longtime owners like to mention.

Put what you know about basement water, sump pumps and past claims on the disclosure form. Keep permits and invoices for any storm repairs, and ask the township whether a flood hazard permit applies to your parcel.

sections.h2: How do Bucks County assessments and tax exclusions affect a Falls sale?
sections.html:
Values and appeals sit with the Bucks County Board of Assessment Appeals at 55 East Court Street, Doylestown. Its 2026 annual appeal deadline fell on August 3, 2026, with a $75 per parcel fee that is not refunded, and any change applies from the 2027 tax year. The board convenes at 10 a.m. on the first and third Tuesdays of the month.

Acceptable proof of value is an appraisal by a Pennsylvania certified appraiser or sales of similar nearby properties from the last 18 months. An owner who bought within 18 months can add the settlement sheet, but it cannot stand alone.

  • Homestead: applications for the tax year starting July 1, 2027 are due March 1, 2027, and a newly recorded deed calls for a fresh application within 45 days.
  • New owners: Act 29 has a purchaser send contact information to the board within 30 days.

Pass the 45-day homestead rule on to your buyer, since a new deed starts the application over.

sections.h2: What transfer tax and state disclosure rules apply in Falls Township?
sections.html:
The state charges a 1% realty transfer tax, which the county Recorder of Deeds gathers with any local tax. Some family transfers and property passed by testate or intestate succession are exempt, and 15% of collections support the Keystone Recreation, Park and Conservation Fund. Ask the Recorder what local rate applies to your price.

For disclosure, 68 Pa.C.S. section 7312 allows a written amendment before the agreement is signed, and section 7307 obliges the seller to notify the buyer if facts change before final settlement. The law defines a material defect as a problem with a significant adverse effect on value or an unreasonable risk to people, and a system near the end of its useful life does not count by that alone. Municipalities may not add disclosure demands beyond the statute, except through ordinances that predate it.

sections.h2: When does a cash sale make sense in Falls Township?
sections.html: It suits owners who want to sidestep repair bids and a buyer's financing contingency. Falls Township cases include an inherited house, a failed heating or sewer system that stalls the resale certificate, a rental unlikely to pass a township inspection, or a move on a fixed date. Measure the offer against a listing's net after repairs and transfer tax.

faqs.q: Is a township home inspection needed to sell in Falls?
faqs.a: No. The township traded its resale inspection for certification of the heating system, chimney, sewer system and electrical panel, leaving any private inspection to buyer and seller.

faqs.q: What if the heating system or another component fails certification?
faqs.a: The certificate of occupancy waits until it is certified. Ask the Code Enforcement Department what repair or permit is needed, or sell as-is to a buyer who will finish the work.

faqs.q: What was the 2026 Bucks County appeal deadline?
faqs.a: August 3, 2026, and it has passed. Annual appeals go to the Board of Assessment Appeals, cost $75 per parcel and alter the assessment from the 2027 tax year.

faqs.q: Do Levittown and Fairless Hills belong to Falls Township?
faqs.a: Parts of both do. Pieces of Fairless Hills and Levittown lie inside the township, and the Morrisville and Yardley post office names also cover some Falls addresses.

faqs.q: How soon can a Falls Township sale close?
faqs.a: The contract sets the date, and a cash buyer has no lender to wait on. Title work, open permits and the resale certificate steps fix the earliest possible day.
